## But what is "learning" and what are "models"?
{{< source "Fairness and machine learning (2023)" url="https://fairmlbook.org/index.html" >}}

:::{.columns}
:::{.column}
![](images/world-data-models-humans-box-2.svg)
:::
:::{.column style="font-size: 80%;"}
<br>

- Models as tools to obtain factual knowledge
- Different types of models: machine learning model, generative AI model, causal model, deductive model
- How does data science and "AI" change how we work with models?
:::
:::


## The Ladder of Causality
{{< source "Judea Pearl (2018)" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Why" >}}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
![](images/ladder-of-causality.png){height=500 }
:::
::: {.column width="65%" style="font-size: 80%;"}
<br>

### Remember:

- Machine learning models are not the only models
- Machine learning models are _only_ based on correlations
- Machine learning _can not_ reason (although LLMs look like they can)
- Read more on [analytical problem with different types of models](https://anthology-of-data.science/posts/analytical-problem-solving/)
:::
:::

## Thinking, Fast and Slow
{{< source "Daniel Kahneman (2011)" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thinking,_Fast_and_Slow" >}}

![](images/kahneman-two-systems.png)

:::{.notes}
- We assume models help us in making rational decisions --> we don't make rational decision
- Framing: the way data and information is presented to us has large impact on the decision we make
:::
